author: SilkyMonstar
quote:
I was so excited. GTA 5 came out when I was in highschool and I played with friends for years. I ignored all the hype and negativity around the game before release and approached it objectively.

My HONEST opinion is this is not a GTA game at its core.
Rankings: 
Gameplay: 5/10; feels like watchdogs with more RP but the wanted system is a nice change.
Story: 3/10. Unlikable protagonists; roughly 50% of the story felt like watching a movie instead of playing a game - and not a good movie either. Contrary to past Rockstar games, most of the characters felt like caricatures of my elementary school teacher's idea of a "good person" and "bad person". What does that mean? "Do unto others what you want them to do to you" and the game's reputation system thoroughly punishes you for being an actual criminal. Yes - you commit crimes - we rob banks, steal cars, raid drug stashes etc. But if you shoot one of the lying drug dealers in the skull while you steal his blood money, you get dinged for "bad behavior". Should've kneecapped him instead, or maybe given him a big old kiss and asked nicely?
Graphics: Good, slightly slow -- re: what my earlier remark about Watchdogs 2.

This feels like it stripped down the GTA franchise for parts. The writing didn't really feel authentically "crime-centric"; it instead felt like a survival game with optional crime mechanics that you can be punished for enjoying. 
In free roam, I didn't feel encouraged to steal cars or rob people: the reward wasn't there and the little demon emoji (telling me I misbehaved) was in its place.

It is certainly a massive departure from the franchise's roots: become a criminal kingpin, get out all the fantasy criminal energy that everyone has. I would return the game if I could.

I wanted to love it, but found myself trudging through. The absolute highest hopes have been crushed along with a piece of my childhood. Certainly cannot recommend a buy.
